Satan agrees that the plan is great but questions who will go due to the danger of escaping hell. Angels guard hell, and even if one leaves, they face the abyss or space where Earth's location is unknown, leading to eternal loss. Satan steps up and volunteers, saying, "I will go."

Our prison in hell is strong, designed with fire that devours us ninefold and gates of burning adamant barring all escape. Escaping hell is immensely difficult; any path leads to the void or unessential night, threatening one's existence in an abortive gulf.

If you can leave hell, you're still in the abyss of the universe, floating eternally without direction. However, I should bear this throne and imperial sovereignty adorned with splendor, armed with power. No danger can deter me from leading us out of this prison. Wherefore do I assume these royalties and not refuse to reign, accepting as much hazard as honor?

You have trusted me to lead you for all eternity, so I will risk my life to prove my worth. High honor sits; go therefore, mighty powers, tear of heaven though fallen, intend at home while here shall be our home. What best may ease the present misery and render hell more tolerable? If there be cure or charm to respite or deceive or slack the pain of this ill mansion, interimmit no watch against a wakeful foe, why I abroad through all the crows of dark destruction seek deliverance for us all. This enterprise none shall partake with me; I am your leader and will go by myself.

You can sip drinks, watch TV, and enjoy yourselves, but I'm your leader. I will go alone to redeem and deliver us from our torment. He is the grand hero describing his ascent almost like souls leaving bodies to heavens. Some believe you meet Satan when you die because he takes souls from the prison world to light. Satan is crucial for secret societies as an initiation ceremony, symbolizing a journey where one must fight for humanity alone.

Satan convinces Eve by saying, "Oh sacred wise and wisdom-giving plant, mother of science, now I feel thy power within me clear not only to discern things in their causes but to trace the ways of highest agents."
